title: G1 library-displacement candidates (recovered functions that are actually SDK/library code)

policy.primary_gate: relocation-masked byte identity between the shipped image at the VA and the pinned NCS 2.5.1 object section .text.<upstream_symbol>, over the FULL upstream section length (not just the Ghidra extent)

confidence.high: full-section relocation-masked byte identity, >=32 distinguishing bytes, plus at least one independent corroborating signal (symbol-name identity / __ASSERT source-path literal / >=3-function upstream-unit cluster) or >=64 distinguishing bytes
confidence.medium: full-section relocation-masked byte identity with 16-31 distinguishing bytes, or full identity where the upstream unit is not currently in the link
confidence.review_required: partial agreement, or competing upstream identities

method: Indexed every .text.<sym> section of every object/archive member of the pinned NCS 2.5.1 app and net builds (5996 app symbols, 2335 net symbols), including the arm-zephyr-eabi 12.2.0 libgcc / newlib-nano multilib archives.

For every catalogued firmware function, compared image bytes at its VA with each upstream section after zeroing the 4-byte window at every relocation offset (the method already used by tools/build_app_bluetooth_stock_adoption.py).
Kept only pairs that agree over the ENTIRE upstream section, then re-scored with the number of bytes that are NOT covered by a relocation.

Corroborated with: recovered-symbol name identity from the naming waves; __ASSERT / log format literals in the function literal pool naming an SDK source path; contiguity clusters of same-unit matches; caller closure from refgraph_{app,net}.json.gz.
Cross-checked against recon/ownership/adoption_manifest.json (553 app / 244 net existing exclusions are not re-listed) and against recon/emulator/reports/golden_boot_trace.json.
